content: 1. A study published in the International Journal of Vitamin and Nutrition Research in 2013 investigated the outcomes of a specific intervention trial. The findings were detailed in volume 83, issue 1, pages 59-66. 2. Quintero MDC and colleagues conducted research on the impact of consuming corn flour with low-level enrichment on children living in rural areas. The results were published in Nutrition Hospitalaria in 2011, volume 26, issue 5, pages 1097-1104. 3. Bagni UV and collaborators examined the effects of weekly rice fortification with iron on anemia prevalence and hemoglobin concentration in children attending public daycare centers in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. This study was published in Cadernos de Saúde Pública in 2009, volume 25, issue 2, pages 291-302. 4. Researchers from the Universidade Federal do Rio de Janeiro explored the effects of rice fortification with iron on anemia among children. 5. Nesamvuni AE, Vorster HH, and colleagues demonstrated that fortification of maize meal improved the nutritional status of African children aged 1-3 years. Their findings were published in Public Health Nutrition in 2005, volume 8, issue 5, pages 461-467. 6. Schumann K and collaborators studied the hematological response to heme iron or ferrous sulfate mixed with refried black beans in moderately anemic Guatemalan preschool children. The results were published in Public Health Nutrition in 2005, volume 8, issue 6, pages 572-581. 7. Lartey A, Manu A, Brown KH, and Dewey KG identified predictors of micronutrient status among sixto twelve-month-old breastfed Ghanaian infants. Their research appeared in the Journal of Nutrition in 2000, volume 130, issue 2, pages 199-207. 8. Lartey A and colleagues conducted a randomized, community-based trial to evaluate the effects of improved, centrally processed complementary foods on the growth and micronutrient status of Ghanaian infants aged 6 to 12 months. The study, which focused on a cereal-legume blend called Weanimix, was published in volume 70, issue 3, pages 391-404. 9. Bovell-Benjamin AC, Allen LH, and Guinard JX assessed toddlers' acceptance of whole maize meal porridge fortified with ferrous bisglycinate. Their findings were published in Food Quality and Preference in 1999, volume 10, issue 2, pages 123-128. 10. Gershoff SN and colleagues conducted a nutrition study in Thailand, examining the effects of rice fortified with lysine, threonine, thiamin, riboflavin, vitamin A, and iron on preschool children. The results were published in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition in 1977, volume 30, issue 7, pages 1185-1195. 11. Gershoff SN and collaborators also studied amino acid fortification of rice in Thailand, providing background and baseline data in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition in 1975, volume 28, issue 2, pages 170-182. 12. Mehta S and colleagues designed a randomized controlled trial to evaluate the effects of consuming ironand zinc-biofortified pearl millet on growth and immune competence in children aged 12-18 months in India. The study protocol was published in BMJ Open in 2017, volume 7, issue 11, article e017631. 13. Stanford University, in collaboration with the Government of Tamil Nadu and other organizations, implemented a large-scale food fortification program aimed at reducing anemia. The initiative was documented in 2020. 14. Researchers from Food and Nutrition, Nestlé, and other institutions studied the effects of nutrient-dense complementary foods on catch-up growth and nutritional status in stunted children. The findings were reported in 2016. 15. Hays N and colleagues evaluated the impact of an iron-fortified complementary food on anemia and nutritional status in infants aged 6-18 months in Ghana. The study was conducted in 2019. 16. A trial conducted in the La Nkwantanang Municipality of the Greater Accra Region assessed the efficacy of an iron-fortified complementary food in improving the nutritional status of children aged 6-18 months. The trial ID was PACTR201906885776793, and the study was completed in 2019. 17. Krebs NF and collaborators investigated the relationship between the size of the exchangeable zinc pool and absorbed zinc in breastfed infants consuming different complementary foods. The findings were published in the FASEB Journal in 2011, volume 25. 18. Araya LH highlighted the importance of food fortification for the health of the Chilean population in a 1994 article in Revista Chilena de Nutrición, volume 22, issue 3, pages 137-143. 19. Arya V discussed the role of calcium in treating nutritional rickets in a 2000 publication. 20. Cros J and Schartner J conducted a trial on food supplementation for children in the Diack canton of Senegal, with results published in 1966 in Bulletin de la Société de Médecine d'Afrique Noire de Langue Française, volume 11, issue 2, pages 193-197. 21. The Pan American Health Organization collaborated with the Instituto de Nutrición y Tecnología de los Alimentos to study food and nutrition interventions for low-income populations in Latin America and the Caribbean. The project summary was published in 1989. 22. Viseshakul D and colleagues conducted a one-year follow-up study on supplementary feeding in hill tribe children aged 1-4 years. The findings were published in the Journal of the Medical Association of Thailand in 1979, volume 62, issue 4, pages 190-200. 23. Viteri FE and collaborators explored iron fortification in developing countries, with their findings published in Progress in Clinical and Biological Research in 1981, volume 77, pages 345-354. 24. Zhao X and colleagues evaluated the efficacy of NaFeEDTA-fortified soy sauce in preventing anemia. The study was published in Wei Sheng Yan Jiu in 2004, volume 33, issue 2, pages 202-204. 25. Zlotkin SH and collaborators studied fractional zinc absorption from zinc-fortified cereals in infants and young children. The findings were published in Pediatric Research in 2000, volume 47, issue 4, page 237A. 26. Dewey KG and colleagues examined the effects of introducing complementary foods at different ages on the iron status of breastfed infants in Honduras. The study included commentary by Garza C and Frongillo EA Jr. and was published in volume 67, issue 5, pages 878-916. 27. Aakko J and collaborators investigated the impact of lipid-based nutrient supplements on gut microbiota in Malawian infants. The randomized trial was published in the Journal of Pediatric Gastroenterology and Nutrition in 2017, volume 64, issue 4, pages 610-615. 28. Aaron GJ and colleagues assessed the acceptability of zinc-fortified complementary foods and breads among young children and adults in Senegal. The findings were published in the Journal of Food Science in 2011, volume 76, issue 1, pages S56-S62. 29. Aboud FE and Akhter S evaluated a responsive stimulation and feeding intervention in Bangladesh through a cluster-randomized trial. The results were published in Pediatrics in 2011, volume 127, issue 5, pages e1191-e1197. 30. Ackatia-Armah RS and colleagues studied the effects of dietary regimens on recovery from moderate acute malnutrition in young Malian children. The findings were published in the FASEB Journal in 2012, volume 26. 31. Ackatia-Armah RS and collaborators also examined the impact of dietary supplements on micronutrient status during recovery from moderate acute malnutrition in young Malian children. The study was published in Annals of Nutrition & Metabolism in 2013, volume 63, page 842. 32. Ackatia-Armah RS and colleagues found that Malian children with moderate acute malnutrition treated with lipid-based dietary supplements experienced greater weight gains and recovery rates compared to those treated with locally produced cereal-legume products. The community-based, cluster-randomized trial was published in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition in 2015, volume 101, issue 3, pages 632-645. 33. A trial in Mexico evaluated the efficacy of different strategies to treat anemia in children. The trial ID was ACTRN126090000061235, and the study was conducted in 2009. 34. Another trial, titled Seeding Through Feeding: Nourishing the Infant Microbiome to Support Immune Health, was registered under trial ID ACTRN12620000026921 in 2020. 35. Agapova SE and colleagues investigated the effects of adding common beans to the diet of Malawian children. While no impact on linear growth was observed, intestinal permeability was reduced. The study was published in the Journal of Nutrition in 2018, volume 148, issue 2, pages 267-274. 36. Ahmad A and collaborators conducted a cluster-randomized control trial in Aceh, Indonesia, to evaluate the effects of nutrition education and multi-nutrient biscuit interventions on the nutritional and iron status of undernourished children aged 6-23 months. The findings were published in Annals of Nutrition and Metabolism in 2019, volume 75, issue 3, page 316. 37. Ahmad A and colleagues also published a study in 2020 in the Journal of Nutritional Science and Vitaminology (Tokyo), volume 66 (Supplement), pages S380-S390, on the same topic. 38. Ahmed T and collaborators developed and tested the acceptability of ready-to-use supplementary food made from locally available ingredients in Bangladesh. The study was published in BMC Pediatrics in 2014, volume 14, article 164. 39. Ahmed T and colleagues reported results from complementary food interventions using local ingredients in a 2017 Nestlé Nutrition Institute Workshop Series publication, volume 87, pages 103-113. 40. Akalu G and collaborators evaluated the effectiveness of quality protein maize in improving the nutritional status of young children in the Ethiopian highlands. The findings were published in Food & Nutrition Bulletin in 2010, volume 31, issue 3, pages 418-430. 41. Ortega Alemán and colleagues compared the effects of high-quality protein maize versus conventional maize on growth and morbidity in undernourished Nicaraguan children aged 1-5 years. The study was published in Archivos Latinoamericanos de Nutrición in 2008, volume 58, issue 4, pages 377-385. 42. Amthor RE and collaborators used home-based therapy with ready-to-use therapeutic food to treat malnutrition in a rural area during a food crisis. The study was published in the Journal of the American Dietetic Association in 2009, volume 109, issue 3, pages 464-467. 43. Anorve-Valdez G and colleagues studied fortified food supplementation in children with reduced dietary energy and micronutrient intake in Southern Mexico. The findings were published in Nutrition Journal in 2018, volume 17, article 76. 44. Arcanjo FPN and collaborators demonstrated that micronutrient fortification at child-care centers reduced anemia in young children. The study was published in the Journal of Dietary Supplements in 2019, volume 16, issue 6, pages 689-698. 45. Argaw A and colleagues conducted a randomized controlled trial in rural Ethiopia to assess the effects of n-3 long-chain PUFA supplementation to lactating mothers and their breastfed children on child growth and morbidity. The findings were published in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition in 2018, volume 107, issue 3, pages 454-464. 46. Ariff SS and collaborators studied zinc absorption and exchangeable zinc pool size in Pakistani infants and toddlers consuming sprinkles and traditional foods. The findings were published in Annals of Nutrition and Metabolism in 2013, volume 63, pages 257-258. 47. Arsenault JE and colleagues found that circulating leptin and ghrelin concentrations were associated with growth in young Peruvian children but were not affected by zinc supplementation. The study was published in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition in 2007, volume 86, issue 4, pages 1111-1119. 48. Arsenault JE and collaborators also reported that additional zinc delivered in a liquid supplement, but not in fortified porridge, increased fat-free mass accrual among young Peruvian children with mild-to-moderate stunting. The study was published in the Journal of Nutrition in 2008, volume 138, issue 1, pages 108-114. 49. Arsenault JE and colleagues identified a dietary pattern with high dairy intake as being associated with linear growth in Peruvian infants. The findings were published in the FASEB Journal in 2016, volume 30. 50. Arya TU conducted a clinical study assessing growth and development in infants using Shashtikshalyadi Churna as a weaning food. The study was published in the International Journal of Research in Ayurveda and Pharmacy in 2014, volume 5, issue 4, pages 439-443. 51. As’ad S and Yusuf I studied the effects of zinc supplementation on TNF-α profiles and diarrhea in severely malnourished children from low-income families in 2003. 52. Asibey-Berkoh E and collaborators evaluated the dual fortification of salt with iron and iodine in women and children in rural Ghana. The study was published in the East African Medical Journal in 2007, volume 84, issue 10, pages 473-480. 53. The Association for the Prevention of HA compared the effects of two treatments on the nutritional and micronutrient status of malnourished children in 2013. 54. Awasthi S and colleagues demonstrated that micronutrient-fortified infant cereal improved hemoglobin status and reduced iron-deficiency anemia in Indian infants. The effectiveness study was published in the British Journal of Nutrition in 2020, volume 123, issue 7, pages 780-791. 55. Badau MH and collaborators studied the production, viscosity, microbiological quality, and sensory properties of complementary food blends made from improved rice cultivars, soybean, and sorghum malt. The findings were published in the Pakistan Journal of Nutrition in 2016, volume 15, issue 9, pages 849-856. 56. Bagni UV and colleagues evaluated the effects of weekly iron chelate fortification of rice on anemia prevalence and hemoglobin concentration in children attending municipal daycare centers in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. The study was published in Cadernos de Saúde Pública in 2009, volume 25, issue 2, pages 291-302. 57. Bajaj M and collaborators assessed the short-term effects of oil supplementation of complementary food on total ad libitum consumption in 6to 10-month-old breastfed Indian infants. The study was published in the Journal of Pediatric Gastroenterology and Nutrition in 2005, volume 41, issue 1, pages 61-65. 58. Baskaran V and colleagues evaluated the acceptability of supplementary foods based on popped cereals and legumes for rural mothers and children. The findings were published in Plant Foods for Human Nutrition in 1999, volume 53, issue 3, pages 237-247. 59. Bauserman M and collaborators conducted a cluster-randomized trial to determine the efficacy of caterpillar cereal as a locally available and sustainable complementary food to prevent stunting and anemia. The study was published in Public Health Nutrition in 2015, volume 18, issue 10, pages 1785-1792. 60. Becroft T and Bailey KV conducted a supplementary feeding trial in New Guinea Highland infants. The findings were published in the Journal of Tropical Pediatrics and African Child Health in 1965, volume 11, issue 2, pages 28-34. 61. Beinner MA and collaborators demonstrated that iron-fortified rice was as efficacious as supplemental iron drops in infants and young children. The study was published in the Journal of Nutrition in 2010, volume 140, issue 1, pages 49-53. 62. Bergmann R and colleagues conducted a prospective, controlled study on preventing iron deficiency in breastfed infants through suitable supplementary food. The findings were published in Monatsschrift Kinderheilkunde in 1989, volume 137, issue 12, pages 775-779. 63. Bernal MJ and collaborators studied the effects of infant cereals with different carbohydrate profiles on colonic function in infants aged 6-12 months. The randomized, double-blind clinical trial was published in the European Journal of Pediatrics in 2013, volume 172, issue 11, pages 1535-1542. 64. Bhandari N and colleagues evaluated the efficacy of three feeding regimens for home-based management of children with uncomplicated severe acute malnutrition in India. The randomized trial was published in BMJ Global Health in 2016, volume 1, issue 4, article e000144. 65. Bhargava A explored the relationship between iron status, malaria parasite loads, and food policies in sub-Saharan Africa. The findings were published in Economics and Human Biology in 2013, volume 11, issue 1, pages 108-112. 66. Bishop WB and collaborators studied the effect of vitamin-enriched bread on the vitamin status of an isolated rural community. The controlled clinical trial was published in the South African Medical Journal in 1996, volume 86, issue 4 (Supplement), pages 458-462. 67. Bisimwa G and colleagues conducted a randomized controlled trial on the use of ready-to-use therapeutic food for treating malnutrition in a rural area during a food crisis. The findings were published in the Journal of the American Dietetic Association in 2009, volume 109, issue 3, pages 464-467.
